subject: Cost prioritization & pilot checklist — PayMora discovery recap
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel@paymora.com>, Maya Singh <maya@paymora.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Cost prioritization & pilot checklist — PayMora discovery recap

Thanks again for the call today — wanted to capture the key cost constraints and a concise pilot checklist so we have aligned next steps. Short version up top, details below.

TL;DR
- Primary goal: validate a production flow for contextual transaction enrichment while staying within an initial Ops budget of ~$18k/month.
- Key pain: current per-request latency and token spend from chat+enrichment is driving >60% of ML infra spend; unbatched synchronous calls amplify cost for high-concurrency peaks.
- Pilot ask: 4-week technical pilot (non-prod) to demonstrate token-econ savings via batching + prefix/KV caching + one quantized model variant. Expected outcome: 30–55% unit-cost reduction depending on batching tolerance.

What we heard (from you)
- Typical request pattern: 1–3 short user prompts plus a 200–700-token enrichment context (transaction + merchant history).
- Peak concurrency: ~150 concurrent requests for the fraud/enrichment flow during mornings. Sustained QPS target for production ~40–60.
- Budget sensitivity: finance comfortable with pilot at ~$15–20k/month but want clear ROI for full rollout decision.

Primary levers we'll test in pilot
1) Batching: group short prompts into micro-batches for the enrichment worker; target batching window 20–50ms.
2) KV/prefix caching: cache merchant embeddings + static metadata to avoid re-sending long prefixes; expect large savings for repeat merchant lookups.
3) Quantized model variant: test int8 / 4-bit quantized weights on compatible model for ~1.4–1.8x token-cost reduction with minimal quality delta for your use case.
4) Routing and model-shim: route non-critical low-latency requests to a lower-cost model tier during spikes.

Immediate asks (what we need from you)
- 7 days: token distribution export (per-request tokens, median and 95th) for the last 30 days (CSV).
- Estimated daily active users and expected QPS for production ramp (just the ranges are fine).
- Decision owner and procurement timeline (who signs pilot SOW).

Proposed next steps
- I will drop a 1-page pilot scope and a short Excel MA (attached) that maps the test matrix to acceptance criteria.
- Can we book a 30-min follow-up on Mon 8/9 or Tue 8/10 to confirm data handoff and procurement path? I proposed both in the calendar invite.

Attachments: paymora-pilot-scope.xlsx (pilot matrix + acceptance criteria), redwood_pilot_ma_template.pdf (simple MA template).

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference


From: Daniel Cho <daniel@paymora.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@paymora.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost prioritization & pilot checklist — PayMora discovery recap
Vanessa — thanks for this write-up, super helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Budget: finance confirmed we can run a pilot for up to $20k/month but need the MA signed and a short line-item budget for tooling / infra.
- Data export: Maya will pull token/export stats by EOD Friday and share a CSV; we will redact any PII.
- Timeline: procurement prefers a 60-day window from pilot close to purchase decision; we need a clear ROI path.

Two asks for the pilot scope:
1) Please include a conservative and optimistic ROI scenario (we care about the downside case).
2) If caching depends on merchant IDs, what are the privacy implications? We need a short note to feed into our security/compliance.
We are OK to proceed with the 4-week technical pilot if we get the MA and the ROI scenarios. I added our procurement lead (CC) but they are out this week — procurement contact will follow next week.
Appreciate the clear checklist — looking forward to the follow-up.
—Daniel
VP, Product — PayMora
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Cost prioritization & pilot checklist — PayMora discovery recap
Karthik / Aditya — forwarding the external confirmation and asks. Quick internal alignment:

What PayMora expects
- Pilot budget: up to $20k/mo; decision window ~60 days after pilot.
- Deliverables: CSV token export (they will provide), MA signed, ROI conservative/optimistic scenarios, note on caching/privacy for merchant IDs.

What I need from Redwood team
1) Karthik — can you draft a 2-slide ROI table (conservative/optimistic) using these pilot levers (batching, KV cache, quantized model)? Use conservative assumptions for batch hit-rate (20%) and optimistic (60%). Include expected effective token-cost reduction and monthly $ impact.
2) Aditya — can you prepare a one-paragraph security note on merchant-ID caching (what is cached, TTLs, encryption-at-rest, how to exclude PII) to feed to their security lead? Keep it <= 150 words.
3) I'll draft the MA and attach the pilot scope; want to keep the SOW simple (non-prod sandbox, success criteria: >=25% unit-cost reduction or end-to-end latency <350ms p50 during micro-batched flow).

Timeline: I want the ROI slides + security note by Mon 8/9 EOD so I can send the MA and book the pilot kickoff for Tues 8/10. They already approved the budget band, so speed here matters.

Forwarded message below for context.

--Vanessa
